Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Saturday is a cold, grey, mostly stable day: high overcast covers the whole area, and thermal strength (w*) is near zero at every site except Daydreams. That site keeps steady thermals of about 150–175 ft/min with a thermal top (height of the mixed layer) of about 1,200–2,400 ft above ground. Southwest winds at Sierra crest height build from about 14–18 knots in the morning to 25–28 knots from 1pm on, raising mountain wave and rotor concerns for the afternoon. This run has weaker thermals and more cloud than the previous run, and the European model agrees with it on crest-level wind, so morning sled rides and a short Daydreams window are the realistic options.

Site Breakdown

McClellan Marginal — Light, mostly launch-aligned southerly wind allows a sled ride, but there are no thermals.
Window: 9am–12pm
Thermal strength is 0 ft/min all day, so expect a glide down rather than a climb. Launch wind is 2–4 mph, mostly from 129–217°, within the southwest/south range. Stable air flows around the lower slope, so the ridge-lift numbers are too high. Wind at 3,000 ft above ground rises to 19–27 mph after noon, so stay in the morning. Launch is at or below freezing (26–36 °F).
Daydreams Marginal — The only site with steady thermals, but the aligned wind window is short and the afternoon brings strengthening crest flow and wave risk.
Window: 9am–11am
Thermal strength is 166–174 ft/min, with a thermal top of 2,439 ft above ground at 9am and 1,792 ft at 10am. Cloud base (where a thermal would form cloud) is about 4,300 ft above launch, so the overcast is high cloud that dims the sun but does not cap climbs. Wind is 8–12 mph from 218–251°, well aligned, with good ridge lift of +126 to +244 ft/min. By 11am wind reaches 20 mph, and from noon it veers to 262–282°, just west of the preferred range, at 11–16 mph. That overlaps the period of strong crest-level flow, so afternoon flights need extra care. Shear is at caution level (8 mph per 100 m at 1,250 ft above ground). Launch temperature is 32–34 °F.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — Wind blows from the west-southwest over the back of this southeast launch all day, with no thermals.
Peak thermal strength 0 ft/min and thermal top at most 1,717 ft above ground. Launch wind is 6–14 mph from 230–263°, well off the preferred southeast direction, and ridge lift is near zero or sinking. Launch temperature is 24–36 °F.
Hallelujah Unfavorable — Wind is never launch-aligned: light and variable in the morning, then 10–11 mph from the south-southeast in the afternoon.
Peak thermal strength is only 47 ft/min, with thermal tops of about 300 ft above ground through midday. The afternoon ridge-lift estimate of +104 to +145 ft/min comes from wind out of 160–171°, which is outside the west/southwest launch range, so evening soaring is not supported. The freezing level reaches launch height and launch temperature is 26–36 °F.
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — Strong west-southwest wind blows over the back of this south/southeast launch, with heavy sink on the launch face.
Launch wind is 13–27 mph from 226–258°, and 30–42 mph at 1,000 ft above ground from 11am. Ridge lift is -450 to -837 ft/min, meaning the launch sits on the downwind side. Thermal strength is 0 ft/min and launch temperature is 25–30 °F.
West McClellan Unfavorable — Wind at launch is mostly south-southwest, crossing this west-facing launch, and there are no thermals.
Launch wind is 6–12 mph from 171–227°, mostly south of the 240–300° range. The brief +316 ft/min ridge lift at 10am comes from a 238° wind that sits right at the edge of the range. Thermal strength is 0 ft/min. Wind shear is at caution level (8 mph per 100 m at 725 ft above ground). Launch temperature is 20–34 °F.
Peavine Mountain Unfavorable — Strong southwest wind of 14–19 mph in the morning rises to 25–30 mph from 1pm, with sink on the launch face.
Ridge lift is -83 to -174 ft/min all day, and wind at 1,000 ft above ground is 26–41 mph from 10am. Thermal strength is at most 8 ft/min, and the air is very stable (4.6 °C/km, slow cooling with height). Launch temperature is 24–27 °F.
Rainbow Ridge Unfavorable — Wind is too light and variable for ridge soaring, and low-level wind shear reaches the hazardous threshold.
The only launch-aligned hour is 2pm, at 8 mph from 58°, but ridge lift of +99 ft/min is well short of the roughly 200 ft/min needed to stay up. Thermals peak at 87 ft/min around noon, when wind is about 1 mph. Wind turns to 10 mph from 211° (over the back) by 4pm. Peak shear is 10 mph per 100 m at 732 ft above ground.
Duck Hill Unfavorable — Wind is southeast all day, the opposite of this west/northwest/north launch.
Launch wind is 4–7 mph from 122–174°, with ridge lift near zero or slightly sinking and no improvement into the evening. Thermal strength is 0 ft/min. Shear is at caution level (8 mph per 100 m at 567 ft above ground).

Hazards

  • Afternoon mountain wave and rotor: Crest-level wind over Reno rises to 25–28 knots from 219–236° between 1pm and 4pm, strong enough to bring wave turbulence, rotor and gusty downslope wind east of the Carson Range and Peavine. The National Weather Service (NWS) Reno also expects low-level wind shear (sudden changes in wind speed or direction near the ground) and mountain wave turbulence regionally after about 1pm Saturday. It expects ridge gusts of 50–70 mph Saturday night into Sunday.
  • Strong wind at high launches: Peavine reaches 25–30 mph from 1pm and Slide Mountain peaks at 27 mph at noon. Wind 1,000 ft above those ridges runs 30–42 mph in the afternoon.
  • Low-level wind shear: Shear reaches the hazardous level at Rainbow Ridge (10 mph per 100 m at 732 ft above ground). It is at caution level at West McClellan, Duck Hill and Daydreams (8 mph per 100 m).
  • Freezing temperatures: Launch temperatures range from about 20 to 39 °F, and the freezing level (7,604 ft above sea level regionally) sits at or below most launches. Expect a stiff, cold wing and cold hands. Cloud base is far above the thermal tops, so climbing into cloud is not a concern today.
  • Morning freezing fog: NWS Reno expects freezing fog at Truckee until about 8–9am Saturday, and patchy freezing fog in Carson Valley and nearby valleys early Saturday morning. Visibility is not modeled here, so check conditions before driving to launch.
  • Incoming weather: The model shows no precipitation during the flying day. NWS Reno expects light showers to reach northeast California Saturday night, with a wetter wave across the Sierra and western Nevada late Sunday morning and afternoon.
